title: Golden income statement uses the following year's interest expense
evidence: The supposedly corrected workbook retains 'Income Statement'!J26 = -'PP&E, Debt, NWC'!E73. J12 identifies 2021, but E73 contains 2022 interest of 108.243085614738. The actual 2021 components are new-debt interest of 117.944214046932 plus existing-debt interest of 45.4220022, totaling 163.366216246932 in D73. The same shift continues across the forecast; N26 references blank I73 and reports zero interest for 2025 despite 90.6177177717491 of senior-note interest that year. This error exists in both the seed and golden workbook, so it is not merely an intentional input defect that the grader permits the agent to repair. J26 and downstream earnings and cash-flow results are checked against the incorrect golden values. The single weight-1 verifier requires all modification cells to match, penalizing the requested thorough correction.
confirmation: Golden 'Income Statement'!J26 = -'PP&E, Debt, NWC'!E73 (108.24, the 2022 value) while D73 holds 2021 interest 163.37, and N26 = -I73 (blank, 0), unchanged from input, so correcting the shift is penalized.

title: Golden workbook retains mixed-year working-capital references
evidence: The seed and golden workbook combine current-year receivables with prior-year inventory, payables and accrued expenses. In 'PP&E, Debt, NWC', I79 identifies 2021 and I80 references 'Balance Sheet'!J15, but I81:I83 reference I17, I29 and I30—the 2020 column. Consequently, golden I84 is 45.28395 rather than the same-year component sum of 22.98053104482. The historical comparison is also misaligned: golden H84 is 22.973 rather than 44.631. This makes golden DCF!C19 report a working-capital increase of 22.31095 instead of a decrease of 21.65046895518, materially understating 2021 free cash flow. These incorrect results are graded modification cells. The sole verifier has weight 1 and requires every modification cell to match, so correcting this identifiable formula error causes an otherwise competent audit to fail.

title: Ground truth leaves real formula errors unfixed, so an agent that fixes them as asked scores 0
evidence: The instruction asks the agent to 'audit and fix this file thoroughly' and lists 'formula logic errors or inconsistencies'. The only differences between the input and the golden file are three fixes: BS J15:N15 and J17:N17 '/12'→'/365', PP&E D21:H21 column shift, and WACC C49 '/1000'→'/1000000'. The golden file still has clear errors that a thorough audit would find. (1) Balance Sheet J70 is '=AVERAGE($D70:$I70)' but K70:N70 are '=AVERAGE($D70:$H70)', which drops the latest historical year. The same pattern appears in Income Statement J45:J49 vs K45:N49. (2) Line Item Metrics H24 is '=H14/AVERAGE('Balance Sheet'!H27:J27)', a 3-column average. I24 averages BS J27:K27 when it should average I27:J27. H35/I35 point at BS J22/K22 instead of I22/J22, one column off from their neighbours. The verifier is all-or-nothing: every modification cell must match and at least 99.8% of regression cells must match. I tested this with the real score_workbooks after a LibreOffice recalculation. Golden plus a fix to BS K70:N70 gives regression 1.0, modification 0.8921 (35 cell errors) → score 0. Golden plus the Line Item Metrics fixes gives modification 0.9917 (4 errors) → score 0. The single weight-1 verifier therefore penalizes correct, in-scope fixes.

title: Broad 'audit and fix thoroughly' prompt and unfixed formula/reference bugs in gt_04_golden.xlsx penalize agents for fixing genuine off-by-one reference errors
evidence: The prompt in problem.py:32 instructs the agent: 'Please audit and fix this file thoroughly. Errors may include but are not limited to: formula logic errors or inconsistencies, hardcoded values that should be formulas, broken cell references, data validation issues, potential calculation errors, inconsistent formatting or naming conventions, best practice violations, and any other issues that could affect accuracy or maintainability.' However, comparing untouched_input_Unit Mismatch_input.xlsx against gt_04_golden.xlsx shows that the golden solution only fixes 3 issues: (1) Balance Sheet!J15:N15 and J17:N17 dividing DSO/DIO by 365 instead of 12, (2) PP&E, Debt, NWC!D21:H21 referencing I13:M13 (2021-2025 CapEx) instead of H13:L13 (2020-2024 CapEx), and (3) WACC!C49 dividing by 1,000,000 instead of 1,000. Meanwhile, gt_04_golden.xlsx leaves multiple genuine off-by-one column-shift errors untouched in graded ranges: (a) On 'PP&E, Debt, NWC', the Total Debt Summary table in D65:H73 sums 2021-2025 debt repayment and interest (e.g., D73 = D61+L61 = 163.366 for 2021, E73 = E61+M61 = 108.243 for 2022, H73 = H61+P61 = 90.618 for 2025), but its headers in D65:H66 link to 'Income Statement'!I11:M12 (2020-2024 instead of 2021-2025), and 'Income Statement'!J26:N26 (2021-2025 Interest Expense) links to -'PP&E, Debt, NWC'!E73:I73 (shifted one column right, pulling 2022-2025 interest into 2021-2024 and pulling empty cell I73 = 0 into 2025, which also causes 'Line Item Metrics'!M29 to evaluate to #DIV/0!); (b) On 'PP&E, Debt, NWC', the Operating Working Capital schedule in C79:M84 has fiscal years 2015-2025 in row 79 ('Income Statement'!D12:N12) and Accounts Receivable in C80:M80 referencing 'Balance Sheet'!D15:N15 (2015-2025), whereas Inventory (C81:M81), Accounts Payable (C82:M82), and Accrued Expenses (C83:M83) reference 'Balance Sheet'!C17:M17, C29:M29, and C30:M30 (2014-2024, shifted one year left). In all 3 production attempts, the agent found and fixed the 3 golden unit/CapEx errors, and also fixed (a) in Unit 1 (and both (a) and (b) in Units 2 and 3) because the prompt explicitly asked to fix broken cell references and formula inconsistencies. Because verify_spreadsheetbench2_cells (weight: 1) requires 100% modification match and 99.8% regression match against gt_04_golden.xlsx, all 3 units scored 0.0 (Unit 1: modification=0.7552, regression=0.9977; Unit 2: modification=0.3651, regression=0.9897; Unit 3: modification=0.3651, regression=0.9905).
